More useful is the forearm manipulation pathway: ED versus theatre reduction, failed reductions, consent and post-manipulation neurovascular checks, which national data show are weak [1758].

topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
usual_baseline: Examination within 24 hours is often done (60–98%) but ECG and bloods lag at 24–72%. The full set is rarely complete: 0% in one ward, 62.8% in another. Specific tests fall far lower: QRISK 2%, urine dip 15–28%, glucose 6–53%. Abnormal ECGs are rarely followed up (3 of 13).
fix_that_works: Checklists and proformas work best. An admission checklist raised bloods 52.9% to 100% and ECG 58.8% to 94.4% [3266]. A proforma took examination from 23% to 100% [3126]. A pre-filled blood request form: full tests 77% to 100% [3295]. Active handover to the physical health nurse: 62.4% to 96.6% [3546]. PDSA cycles on a rehab ward: 92% overall [1361].
fix_that_fails: An A3 poster gave small gains: examination 34.5% to 47%, all three components 33% [3260]. Undescribed recommendations moved ECG within 24 hours only from 52% to 62% [3281]. Chaperone documentation stayed at 14%, with no choice of chaperone gender offered [3272].
consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, with the same result across trusts. Don't repeat an admission-checks audit. Audit what happens to abnormal results instead: abnormal ECGs followed up, raised HbA1c acted on, vitamin D re-checked after loading. Transfers and duty-doctor admissions do worse and are worth targeting.

usual_baseline: Full protocol analgesia is uncommon: 0/27 [1529] and 34% [1321] after joint replacement. Pain was well managed in 30% [2453]. NSAIDs are under-used: 28% of eligible patients [2611], ibuprofen often omitted without a reason [1529]. IV paracetamol is used when oral would do [2611].
fix_that_works: Electronic order sets work. A prescribing order set: total compliance 0% to 58% [1529]. An EPR powerplan: 34% to 61%, with 87% of compliant patients using it [1321]. Posters and teaching: 30% more regular oral opioids on day 0 [1298].
fix_that_fails: Teaching, leaflets and emails: WHO ladder compliance fell from 83.3% to 50.9% [2043]. A departmental talk: adequate pain control only 30% to 46%, anti-emetics down from 92% to 82% [2453]. Ibuprofen stayed at 58% despite an order set [1529].
consultant_advice: Build the protocol into electronic prescribing and audit its use. Education alone has not held. More useful measures are NSAID omission without a reason and IV paracetamol when oral is possible, both simple to fix.

usual_baseline: Anaemia is common and rarely treated. 71% below Hb threshold but 6.7% given iron [2128]; 38% operated with Hb <130 and 7% treated [1387]; iron studies 8% and screening 6 weeks before surgery 3.95% [1590]; 18% of anaemic colorectal patients given IV iron [2046].
fix_that_works: Governance presentation and a departmental plan to treat to Hb 130: operated with Hb <130 fell from 38% to 21%; anaemias investigated 11% to 80% [1387]. Education plus publicising a day-case iron pathway: IV iron 18% to 60%, transfusion 45% to 20% [2046][2174].
fix_that_fails: Actual treatment lagged investigation: attempted treatment rose only from 7% to 20%, not significant (p = 0.279) [1387].
consultant_advice: Everyone finds untreated anaemia. Audit timing instead: whether Hb is checked early enough, at least 6 weeks before surgery, to treat it. Measure iron given and Hb reached, not just screening.

usual_baseline: Fasting is almost always too long: clear fluids mean 10.5 hours, solids 15.8 hours; 62% 'nil by mouth from midnight' [1655]. Only 39% got their usual medicines while fasting [1644]. Unnecessary tests are routine: 91% of ASA 1–2 abscess patients had bloods [2685]; 81% of coagulation screens inappropriate [2279].
fix_that_works: Posters and dissemination: abscess bloods 91% to 27%, £2,151 to £406 [2685]. Coagulation appropriate 19% to 56% [2279]. Decision aid cut ASA 2 FBCs by 75.0% [2859]. Patient leaflets: clear fluid fasting median 10 to 3 hours [2380]. Drug trolley posters: correct medicines 39% to 61% [1644]. Liquid fasting 10% to 60% [2088].
fix_that_fails: SipTilSend lapsed: fluid fasting rose from 3 h 45 min to 11.2 hours despite reinforcement [1191]. Solid fasting did not improve: 5% to 0% [2088], median 12.5 to 11 hours [2380].
consultant_advice: Fasting audits are common and relapse fast, so measure sustainability months later rather than another baseline. Unnecessary bloods before minor surgery are a quick, cheap win with cost figures. Omitted critical medicines while nil by mouth are less audited and more important.

usual_baseline: Errors are widespread. One audit of 228 prescriptions found errors in every field except timings [3214]. Generic names in 40.6% and block letters in 17% [3403]. Missing dose, frequency, strength and dates in 156 charts [3462]. In a community team, 65% of prescriptions uploaded and 19% in the clinic register [3607].
fix_that_works: BNF guidance presented and copies placed at nursing counters: generic names 40.6% to 84.69%, block letters 17% to 71.42%, start date 82.8% to 99.18% [3403]. A faculty workshop and mandatory teaching gave improvement across all areas, but no figures were given [3462]; nor for [1797].
fix_that_fails: Presentation and re-training made things worse: GMC number errors up 20.33%, doctor's name up 16.87%, indication up 12.94% [3214]. The trust then issued stamps with GMC number and name.
consultant_advice: Common and easy, and several audits report no figures, which makes them useless. If you do it, report numbers per field. Stamps or electronic prescribing will fix identifiers better than teaching, so audit the fields that need clinical thought, such as indication.

usual_baseline: Indication and maximum 24-hour dose are near 100% [3340][3522][3636]. Review is the gap: review date 0/32 [3636], ward round review 3.2% [3522], reviewed in last 7 days 25% [3340]. Unused PRN not stopped: 0% [3522], 0/8 [3636], 5 of 21 still active [3664]. PRN protocol standards met in 53% [3096].
fix_that_works: Induction teaching, weekly pharmacist discussion, chart prompts and weekly MDT PRN review: reviewed in last 7 days 25% to 56% [3340]. After a serious incident, ward round reviews rose from 3.2% to 64.5% and minimum dose interval from 64.5% to 93.5% [3522].
fix_that_fails: Stopping unused PRN only reached 22.2% and review of regularly used PRN 28.5% [3522]. Minimum dose documented rose only from 10.7% to 24%, and no item reached the 100% standard [3340].
consultant_advice: Don't audit indication or maximum dose; they are nearly always met. Audit review and discontinuation. One Trust added an automatic 14-day review date in EPMA [3636]; re-auditing whether that works would be more useful than a new baseline.

usual_baseline: About half are checked: 23.33% [3142], 41–52% [1363, 3379], 43–47% [3224, 3612], up to 80.6% [3381]. Baseline before starting is 43–44.4% [3191, 3224]; 12-week check 12% [3623]. Raised results are often not acted on: action 27.3% [3191], 41.7% [3381]; symptoms assessed 9.1% [3191].
fix_that_works: Trust-wide recommendations after a 2021 audit (not described): monitoring 47% and 43% to 100% (n=160) [3612].
fix_that_fails: Re-audit with no described intervention: 41% to 51% [3379]; 69% to 76% on admission [3657]. Even at 100% testing, raised prolactin was managed in only 4 of 9 [3612]. Symptom documentation stayed poor [3657].
consultant_advice: Testing rates are well documented and ten audits say the same. The real gap is what happens after a raised result: symptoms asked, action taken, repeat test. Audit that, with a named pathway or electronic prompt, and re-audit it.

usual_baseline: Rationale is usually recorded (85–100%). Plans to reduce or stop are not: timescale for stopping 29% [3469], reduce/stop plan 10–17% [3709], no clear indication for 50.6% of antipsychotics [3608]. Monitoring and consent are weak: consent and monitoring under 10% [3216], metabolic monitoring 0% [3292]. One CAMHS service scored 98% [3383].
fix_that_works: Repeated cycles in one ID team: metabolic monitoring 0% to 95%, risk assessment 68% to 100%, target behaviour described 74% to 100% [3292].
fix_that_fails: Side-effect discussion at initiation fell from 73% to 38% after criteria changed [3440]. Consent stayed low (19% to 46%), and single drug therapy 19% to 34% [3292]. Mental health evaluation fell from 87% to 60% [3292].
consultant_advice: Thirteen audits, only two re-audited. Documenting a rationale is solved. Audit whether a reduce-or-stop plan with a timescale exists and is acted on, and count actual dose reductions, not just reviews.

usual_baseline: Most patients are on medication: 81–96% [3067][3308][3312]. Antipsychotics over 4 weeks without psychosis 86% [3219]; 80% had no licensed indication, mean 36.79 months, with no physical review [3308]. Time-limited prescribing 39.4%, written information 4.2% [3312]. PRN over one week in 21 of 50 inpatients [3067].
fix_that_works: A trust prescribing guidance for personality disorder [3219] raised documented reasons for antipsychotics from 43% to 69% and medication reviews from 90% to 100%.
fix_that_fails: After the same guidance, antipsychotics over 4 weeks without psychosis rose from 86% to 91%, Z-hypnotics over 4 weeks from 13% to 37.5%, benzodiazepines over 4 weeks from 28% to 38%, and crisis plans fell from 87% to 79% [3219]. Review quality was unchanged.
consultant_advice: Only one loop is closed, and guidance alone did not cut long-term prescribing. Don't just count prescriptions. Audit whether antipsychotics are reviewed with a plan to stop, whether physical health checks happen, and whether patients get written information, which is almost never given.

usual_baseline: Positioning standards are often missed. Calibration marker balls were present in 44–45% [1322, 1727]. Lateral ankle talar domes superimposed in 61% [1724]; wrist piso-scapho-capitate relationship 50% [1745]. 69/100 arthroplasty films were adequate [1633]. Only 23.09% of shoulder AP views met criteria and 21.17% had an axillary view [1667].
fix_that_works: Posters plus teaching by an associate specialist raised talar dome superimposition from 61% to 85% [1724] and wrist relationship from 50% to 82% [1745]. Posters, a radiographer presentation and a mandatory checklist raised marker ball presence from 45% to 78% [1727]. A protocol and ordering rota raised timely templating films from 20% to 70% [1698]. Guidelines and feedback raised adequate arthroplasty films from 69/100 to 84/100 [1633].
fix_that_fails: Calibration marker compliance fell to 44% after an earlier improvement from 64% to 73% [1322]. Pubic symphysis centring reached only 47% and GT/LT level 43% [1633]. Overall marker compliance change was not significant (59% to 80%, p=0.132) [1727].
consultant_advice: Radiograph positioning audits improve quickly with posters and joint teaching of radiographers and doctors, but gains fade [1322]. Involve the radiography team from the start and build checks into the request or checklist. More useful is measuring whether poor films led to repeat exposure or missed injury, which none of these assessed.

usual_baseline: Choice and dose of drug are usually right. Documentation around it is weak. Protocol steps followed in 60%; indication documented in 50%; reasons for IM medication and side-effect monitoring 25.42%. Post-RT monitoring is the most common failure: full observations in 33%, or not evident at all. Junior doctors often do not know the protocol.
fix_that_works: A structured pre-RT checklist with staff education: pre-RT workup 47% to 85%, reassessment before repeat dosing 42% to 92%, de-escalation 71% to 92% [3590]. At re-audit in older patients, indication documented rose from 50% to 88.8% [3407].
fix_that_fails: Post-RT monitoring stayed poor at re-audit: still not evident in older patients [3407], and below standard with debriefing, medication review and incident reporting in an acute ward [3656]. Advance directives were absent in both audits [3656].
consultant_advice: Don't just audit drug choice; it is usually correct. Audit post-RT physical observations and debriefing, which stay poor after re-audit. On medical and older people's wards, check junior doctors' knowledge of the protocol, which was limited [3382].

usual_baseline: Many transfusions fall outside threshold. Only 21.4% met NICE thresholds and targets [1254]; 73.5% were inappropriate [1294]; 40.2% of units followed NICE [2539]; 34% used a threshold below 70 g/L in critical care [2967]. Back-to-back units without reassessment were 20.5% [2539]. Out-of-hours units were appropriate in 70.6% [2638].
fix_that_works: Teaching and ward posters of thresholds: back-to-back units 20.5% to 4.51%, reactions 2 to none, saving about £5493 a year [2539]. Teaching and an induction booklet: TACO assessment 58.8% to 90.9% [1294].
fix_that_fails: After teaching, 45.5% of transfusions were still inappropriate [1294], and only 50.4% of units followed NICE [2539]. Both re-audits were small.
consultant_advice: Worth doing but the finding is well known. Measure single-unit prescribing and reassessment between units, and reasons for higher thresholds, such as a loosely defined 'coronary history' with no ACS [1254]. Pre-operative iron treatment was 7% and is a better target.

usual_baseline: CT KUB within target is usually good, 93–100% [2383][2464][2495][2691], but not everywhere (335 of 705 within 14 hours [2273]). Serum calcium 21–51% [2691][2464][2624], urate 2.6–4%, NSAIDs 52–55% [2464][2495], dietary advice 8.7–17% [2495][2624].
fix_that_works: Renal order-set and stone diet leaflet: calcium 77.9% to 94.7%, NSAIDs 54.5% to 71.9%, dietary advice 8.7% to 39.4% [2495]. Email reminders and a handover-sheet note: calcium 21% to 72% [2691]. Hot URS theatre: treatment within 48 hours 35% to 53%, dietary advice 17% to 72% [2624].
fix_that_fails: Updated NSAID dosing and pathway: NSAIDs fell 87% to 50% on six patients [2383]. After teaching, only 26.4% were seen in clinic within 4 weeks [2049]. Dietary advice stayed low at 39.4% [2495].
consultant_advice: CT timing is done and usually met; don't audit it again. Audit what happens after the ED: time to definitive treatment, stent use without indication, and follow-up clinic waits. Use an order-set for calcium.

topic: Resuscitation and physical health equipment on psychiatric wards
usual_baseline: Equipment is usually partly available: 66–90% of standards met. Missing or expired adrenaline, suction and masks in 7/10 locations [3380]; 70% of weekly checklists wrong. One learning disability unit had no trolley [3070]. Small items such as testing pins, Snellen charts and ophthalmoscopes are borrowed between wards [3671].
fix_that_works: Equipment boxes in clinic rooms: availability 66% to 73.5% [3093]. Weekly checks, maintenance registration and complete sets: resuscitation equipment 94.2% to 99.2% [3244]. An updated local protocol left trolleys better stocked [3070].
fix_that_fails: Physical health equipment fell from 83.8% to 76.6% despite the same interventions [3244]. Secure wards still lagged controls [3093]. Items added to trolleys were hard to find [3070].
consultant_advice: A quick audit, but resuscitation kit tends to improve once weekly checks are enforced. Physical health kit is the neglected side. Measure whether it is working and used, with a named checker, rather than just counting items.

topic: Risk assessment documentation in mental health
usual_baseline: Risk to self and others is usually recorded, but depth is poor. Junior clerking included risk in 40–70%. Absconding, historical risk and risk to the opposite sex are often missed. Structured suicide assessment was near zero: C-SSRS 0.8%, safety plan 0.8%. Service user involvement 16%. Annual review 81.8%, lower for doctors than nurses.
fix_that_works: Staff education, ward checklists and ward-round reminders: risk assessment within 24 hours 64% to 92%, review before discharge 40% to 84%, update before discharge 40% to 80% [3691]. An email with updated guidance: annual CRAFT 81.8% to 86.4%, medical 77.6% to 83.6% [3642].
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
consultant_advice: Checking that a risk assessment exists is overdone. Audit its quality: structured suicide assessment, safety planning, historical risk and whether the patient took part. Samples here are often small (10–37), so aim for more.

usual_baseline: Rationale and timing of review usually above 90%. Medical review within 1 hour is poor: 20% [3297], 34% [3212][3305], 39% [3483], 44% [3404]. Content gaps: medication side effects 0% [3651], risk to self 5% [3404]. No review met all eight criteria [3651]. Independent reviews by an Approved Clinician often missing [3280].
fix_that_works: A seclusion review template in the documentation plus teaching: 95–100% [3152]. An integrated care pathway: MHC rule compliance from 3–100% to 69–100% [3064]. Education in secure LD wards: review within 1 hour 34% to 66%, medications 20% to 72% [3212]. Huddles and weekly meetings: consultant review within 24 hours from under 70% to over 90%, average seclusion 30 to 20 hours [3129].
fix_that_fails: Four PDSA cycles of proforma, email and teaching: 75% to 83%, minimal change on the SPC chart [3576]. Teaching and posters: side effects 0% to 19%, steps to end seclusion 25% to 23% [3651]. A previous audit led to no change [3297]. Just under half still monitored per guidelines [3129].
consultant_advice: Medical review documentation has been audited many times. Teaching alone gives small gains; a mandatory template works better. More useful: audit out-of-hours timing, Approved Clinician independent review [3280], seclusion room standards [3485], or seclusion duration.

usual_baseline: Acute care is mostly done: pre- and post-reduction x-rays 88–97% [1212, 1713], MUA successful 98% [1713]. Follow-up is weaker: appropriate imaging 40–43.3% [1212, 1240], shoulder specialist 40.3–50% [1212, 1240]. Post-reduction views adequate in only 22.7% [1729]. Triage to reduction x-ray 2 hours 25 min [1571]; mean time to reduction 152 minutes [1713].
fix_that_works: A Shoulder Reduction Bench with nurse practitioner training, a written protocol and an online video: triage to reduction x-ray 2 h 25 min to 1 h 54 min, triage to discharge 3 h 22 min to 2 h 30 min, sedation 57% to 18% [1571].
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
consultant_advice: Only one loop is closed here. Pre- and post-reduction x-ray rates are high, so don't re-audit them. Audit whether post-reduction films are truly orthogonal, and whether first-time dislocations reach a shoulder surgeon with the right imaging.

usual_baseline: Early CT is good: 88–98.3% [2348][2561]. Water-soluble contrast is patchy: 12% [2348], 37% [2402], 64% [2170], 80% [2092]. Delays to surgery are long: 4 days [2402], 2.4 days [2561]. Operative mortality 14% [2417][2561].
fix_that_works: Flowchart plus a theatre slot within 72 hours: SBO operative mortality 14% to 5% [2417]. Presenting NASBO recommendations at governance: water-soluble contrast 12% to 44%, no oral intake >5 days 44% to 17% [2348].
fix_that_fails: Nutritional assessment did not improve after governance presentation: malnourished identified 6% then 5% [2348].
consultant_advice: CT timing is already good and not worth auditing. Measure water-soluble contrast use, time to theatre after failed conservative care, and nutrition. Guaranteed theatre access is the fix with an outcome to show for it.

topic: Smoking cessation in mental health inpatients
usual_baseline: Status is usually asked (66.7–92%, but 31% on older adult wards [3650]); treatment lags. NRT offered 20–25% [3582][3692]; dual NRT 0% [3451]; NRT within 30 minutes 0% [3650]; side-effect monitoring 0% [3582]. Detailed assessment under 10% [3205]. Cessation in discharge letters: one of 219 [3707], 3.3% [3582].
fix_that_works: Staff education and clerking reminders [3692]: status 66.7% to 93.3%, brief advice 33.3% to 84.6%, NRT 25% to 76.9%, referral 8.3% to 53.8%. A ward poster cut incorrect NRT prescribing from 22% to 0% [3148]. A standard smoking and vaping checklist gave full histories in both new admissions [3698].
fix_that_fails: A re-audit with no intervention fell from 71.88% to 36.84% assessed; after a shared presentation it reached only 57.14%, with under 40% assessed in detail, blamed on doctor rotation [3205].
consultant_advice: Many baselines; asking about smoking is mostly fine. The gaps are prompt and adequate NRT, dual NRT, vaping and plans at discharge. Audit time to first NRT, dose adequacy, and whether the discharge letter carries a cessation plan and medication adjustment [3707].

topic: Substance misuse screening in mental health patients
usual_baseline: About half to two-thirds of patients are asked about substance use: 69% [3115], 7/12 [3333], nearly half not asked [3238]. Older people, women and ward referrals are asked least (over 80s 0%) [3115]. Drug screening was documented in 57.5% and offered to 52.5% [3473]. Specialist service involvement is weakest (62.06% on admission, 42.8% at discharge) [3514].
fix_that_works: A training session on results and NICE recommendations raised screening from 69% to 93%, over 80s from 0% to 60% and ward referrals from 33.3% to 85% [3115]. At re-audit, 78% were asked about alcohol and 77% about drugs, with documented advice up 21% [3238].
fix_that_fails: No intervention was followed by no improvement. Items that stayed poor: at re-audit, 27% with identified misuse had no intervention documented [3238]. Over 80s reached only 60% after training [3115].
consultant_advice: Asking the question is easy to improve with teaching. The gap lies in what happens next: advice, brief intervention and specialist referral, and reasons for refused drug tests [3473]. Audit the action taken for positive screens, and include older patients and women.

topic: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation
usual_baseline: Under half fully documented: 36–46% in most units. Individual nerves are worst, anterior interosseous as low as 10%. Many notes say only 'NV intact'. Post-operative nerve checks were 9.7% in one unit. After manipulation in ED, 63.2% had no documentation.
fix_that_works: A proforma, best built into clerking. Electronic pro forma: 86–95% across nerves, sustained at 12 months [1142]. Simple proforma: under 40% to 70% [583] [1270]. Proforma plus teaching: 45.8% to 76.5% [578]; ED nerve function 37.9% to 72.7% [1654]. Consultant-led joint ED and orthopaedic teaching: ED specific documentation 38.9% to 82.9% [1628].
fix_that_fails: A single awareness talk: detailed neurological findings 38.8% to 54.2%, not significant [1747]. With no stated fix, 36% only reached 45% [1211]. Pre-op nerve documentation stayed at 50% [1654], and post-manipulation documentation stayed poor, 31.8% still with none [1628].
consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, with the same finding and fix. Don't repeat it unless your unit has no proforma. Audit whether the proforma is still used a year on, or audit documentation after manipulation and after surgery, which stay poor even when admission notes improve.
revises_seed_card: Supracondylar fracture nerve and vessel documentation

usual_baseline: Prophylaxis is almost always given. Duration and choice fail. Full compliance ranged 23.7% [2316] to 74.1% [1333]. Correct agent 43.5–65.4% [2316, 1712]. Duration too long in 21–25% [2074, 2316]. Postprocedural doses were appropriate in 48.3% [1591]. Post-incision dosing ran 18.9% [2445] and 26% in appendicectomy [1594].
fix_that_works: Changes built into theatre routine work. Posters and stickers: correct MRSA-unknown agent 18% to 94% [1541]. A new protocol with posters: courses cut to 24 hours, stay 3.33 to 2.04 days, no SSI [1607]. Sign-in/time-out edits and a duration sticker: mean duration 70.4 to 28.2 hours, correct agent 43.5% to 65.3% [2445].
fix_that_fails: MRSA eradication stickers: 1% to only 8% [1541]. Presenting at governance: appropriate prophylaxis 78% to 83%, with more incomplete courses [1255]. Full compliance stayed at 39.8% after a year of QI [2445]. Administration time stayed poorly documented [2887].
consultant_advice: Don't audit whether prophylaxis was given; it nearly always is. Audit duration after surgery and choice of agent, and add a prompt to the WHO time-out or drug chart. Recording SSI and dosing errors, as one large audit did [1333], adds more value.

usual_baseline: SSI rates vary widely: 6.76% in emergency general surgery [2512], 14.5% across a district hospital [1267], 29% in elective colorectal surgery [2535], deep infection 3.6% after hip fracture [1404]. Prevention steps patchy: perioperative showering 44%, intra-op antibiotics 14.29% [2512].
fix_that_works: Changing gloves and instruments before abdominal closure, then team education: 29% to 23% to 15%, sustained 6 months [2535]. Fixing infection-policy shortfalls: deep infection 3.6% to 1.1% [1404]. Antibiotic flow-chart for diabetics: 7/14 to 16/19 given prophylaxis, 0 diabetic infections [2335].
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
consultant_advice: Active follow-up matters: 38 SSIs were found only by telephone call [1267], so ward-based counts undercount. Pick one specialty, follow patients after discharge, and test one specific measure such as glove and instrument change.

topic: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
usual_baseline: Request-to-scan often meets targets, but presentation-to-MRI is long: mean 12.5 hours [1660], median 5.9 hours [1704], 438 minutes [1318]. Only 15% referred with an MRI done [1279]. CES confirmed in only 7–18% of referrals or scans. Documentation of perianal sensation 72% and spinal plan 20% [1621].
fix_that_works: An orthopaedic middle grade in ED: mean MRI wait 12.5 to 8 hours, same-day discharge 29% to 58% [1660]. Referral 176 to 60.8 minutes, MRI 438 to 185 minutes [1318]. Teaching and SBAR template: perianal sensation 72% to 97% [1621]. SOP and triage work: unnecessary MRIs 38% to 18% [1704].
fix_that_fails: Three PDSA cycles left median presentation-to-MRI at 5.7 hours; scanners closing at 20:00 blocked it [1704]. Senior ED discussion fell 61.9% to 9% and documented spinal plan 20% to 0% [1621].
consultant_advice: Time to MRI depends on scanner hours and staffing more than on trainees. Audit the whole pathway from arrival, not just request-to-scan, which usually passes. The yield of scans and discharge safety are more useful than another timing audit.

usual_baseline: Time and pressure are usually recorded (time 56–95%, pressure 20.5–88%). Skin condition, isolation and exsanguination are almost never recorded: 0–43%. Pressures often exceed BOAST limits: within standard in only 24–35% in two audits, over in 47.5–70% in another. Fixed 250 mmHg used in 95.3% [2626]. Time over 120 minutes is rare.
fix_that_works: A mandatory electronic op note template: skin 37% to 69%, pressure documented 71% to 94%, within limit 25% to 75% [1664]. EPR auto-text: skin 0% to 64.3%, exsanguination 5.6% to 42.9% [1665]. A smart phrase with automatic SBP calculation: 17% to 62% [1677]. A template and laminated reminders: skin isolation 80% to 100% [2764].
fix_that_fails: Education alone gave little change: exsanguination 9.8%, skin 5.2% [1665]. EPR roll-out without a template dropped compliance to 17% [1677]. Teaching, checklist and posters left most items under 50%; time stayed at 56% [1759]. Pressures within standard did not improve with the proforma (13.0% lower limb) [1665].
consultant_advice: Well audited, with a known fix: a mandatory electronic template. Don't repeat the documentation audit. Audit the pressures actually used, cuff sizing and paediatric pressures, which stay poor even when documentation improves.

fix_that_works: Senior ownership and ward round checks. Regular frailty consultant review: 58% to 83% [2697]. Local pathway letting F1s complete TEPs plus post-take ward round reminders: 69.5% to 88.2% [1661]. Ward round check, SHO completion at clerking and training: 40.47% to 64.86% [2220]. Education and handover reminders: 0% to 40% [2278].
fix_that_fails: Email: 6.18% to 5% [2718]. Departmental presentation and a target: 15% to 17% [2600]. Posters: 39.6 to 34.6 hours, not significant [2658]. Take-list column then poster and teaching: 31% to 33% [2343]. Correct TELP 11.1% to 16.7% [2106]. Completion within 48 hours fell from 47.82% to 35.29% [1661].
consultant_advice: Heavily overdone in surgery, with emails and posters failing again and again. Don't repeat a completion count. Audit form quality, such as capacity and discussion, or test senior review on the post-take ward round and whether it lasts.

usual_baseline: Documentation is very poor. ARAF completed in 3% [3220], 0% dual-signed [3680]; 4/25 on the programme [3139]. Teratogenicity discussed in 3% [3442]; full counselling 24.5% [3622]. Contraception advice 0% [3442], 15% [3680]. Men are worst: risk discussion 17%, contraception 3% [3680].
fix_that_works: Structured outpatient reviews, MHRA materials, a live ARAF tracker and education: men's risk discussion 17% to 87%, contraception 3% to 83%, consent 20% to 87% [3680]. Phoning and emailing teams: ARAF 3% to 54% [3220]. Teaching: teratogenicity 3% to 47.6%, pregnancy test 65.6% to 90% [3442].
fix_that_fails: After teaching, discussion of benefits barely moved (21% to 23.8%) and contraception education reached only 38.1% [3442]. ARAF completion still reached only 54% [3220].
consultant_advice: Baselines are uniformly poor, so another snapshot adds little. The 2024 guidance covering men is barely audited and gave the biggest gains. Audit a tracker-led system, or whether patients were switched to alternatives.

usual_baseline: Doses and level timing are mostly right: correct starting dose 100% [2972][2982], levels at correct time 87–90%. Levels are often out of range: first levels in range 7–33% [2996][2972][3012]. Abnormal levels are not always acted on: 3 of 4 low levels ignored [2982].
fix_that_works: Continuous infusion in neonates: levels in range 28% to 62% [2980]. New paediatric guideline with pharmacist input: in range at 48 hours 7% to 40%; out-of-range levels reviewed 40%, 80% with pharmacist [2996].
fix_that_fails: Electronic prescribing templates and recirculated guideline improved dose frequency (75.9% to 92.6%) but therapeutic first concentration fell from 24.1% to 19.2% [3012]. Still over 80% not in range.
consultant_advice: Prescribing compliance is not the problem. The dosing regimen itself often misses range. Audit first-level attainment and the response to out-of-range levels, and test continuous infusion or pharmacist-led adjustment.

usual_baseline: Testing is patchy: 0% [3345], 56% [3007], 56.4% [3123], 89% [3183]. Deficiency is common: 64% insufficient [1159]; only 25% adequate [3183]; 68.18% deficient or inadequate [3345]. Dosing is often wrong: correct dose 21.4%, 41.4% no dose when indicated [1360]. Prophylaxis prescribed 16% [3472], 1 of 10 [3497].
fix_that_works: A pre-populated admission blood form including vitamin D: testing 0% to 86.67%, then 90% sustained in round three [3345]. Psychoeducation and a clinic room poster: supplementation 1 of 10 to 9 of 10 [3497]. A simplified poster and flow chart: prophylaxis 16% to 31% [3472].
fix_that_fails: Policy update and education in a frailty ED changed nothing: 65% to 61% [1826]. In the CAMHS unit, level monitoring stayed at 5 of 10 over three cycles [3497].
consultant_advice: Mostly single-cycle audits across very different settings. The default test on the admission form is the fix that sticks. Audit whether deficient patients get the correct dose and a repeat level, not just whether a test was sent.

usual_baseline: Initial assessment is often fair, but reassessment is almost absent: 0% [1206] and 0.13% within 24 hours [1690]. Risk assessment for immobilised lower limbs was 32–45% [1358, 1228]. Operation notes lacked any VTE plan in 42% [1642]. Psychiatric wards did worst: 13% [3109], 0–8% [3176].
fix_that_works: An automated EPMA prompt raised 24-hour reassessment from 0.13% to 74% [1690]. A redesigned pathway with an electronic discharge block raised ED risk assessment from 32% to 93.1% [1358]. A teaching half-day and written policy raised discharge chemoprophylaxis from 57% to 98% [1642]. A discharge letter template reached 95% [1207]. A proforma on drug charts reached 100% [3109].
fix_that_fails: Teaching, posters and an EPR dropdown raised reassessment only to 3% within 24 hours [1206]. Teaching did not change prophylaxis after long arthroscopy (50% to 55%, p=1.0) [1718]. An aspirin policy reached 93% but symptomatic VTE stayed at 6.4% [1520]. Compliance dipped to 86% after rotation [1524].
consultant_advice: VTE assessment audits are very common. Initial assessment is usually fine because it is mandatory; target the gaps instead: reassessment at 24 hours, the plan in the operation note, and discharge prescriptions. Electronic prompts and templates beat teaching. Where possible, record VTE events, not just forms completed [1520].

usual_baseline: Completion of risk assessment varies widely, from 0–39% to over 90%. Completion is not accuracy: one trust had 72.1% completed but 15.4% accurate. Re-assessment at 48 hours is poor (36.1%). Mechanical prophylaxis is the weakest item: TEDs given to 5% of eligible ENT patients, appropriate in under 40% elsewhere.
fix_that_works: Changes to the system work best. Electronic assessment, mandatory teaching and clerking prompts: completion 16.67% to 100% [2416]. Drug chart checkboxes for weight and renal function: correct doses 29/36 to 37/38 [2219]. A handover checkbox and posters with forms attached: form use 0% to 70% [2475]. Mandatory junior doctor training: prescribing accuracy 41.2% to 79.5% [2195].
fix_that_fails: Posters and reinforcement: insufficient prophylaxis rose from 40% to 50%, stocking non-compliance 37.4% to 46.4% [2158]. Five years of teaching and reminders: documentation fell from 92% to 53% [2172]. Teaching did not reduce omitted doses (9.3%) [2549] and delayed assessments rose 16.3% to 35.7% [2676]. Assessment accuracy stayed at 34.5% [2195].
consultant_advice: Heavily overdone. Completion alone is not worth auditing again. Audit accuracy instead: correct risk category, correct dose for weight and renal function, and stockings actually worn. Re-assessment at 48 hours and over-prescribing, as in plastic and breast surgery, are measured far less often.

usual_baseline: Hip fractures are nearly always allowed to weight-bear (95.7–98.5%) [1247, 1286]. Other fractures are not: 32.3% of non-hip fragility fractures [1630], 57% after femoral fixation [1767], 21% after ankle fixation [1562]. Operation note documentation against BOAST is poor: 6% [1309] and 0–14% [1323]. Restrictions rarely give reason or duration.
fix_that_works: No successful fix with re-audit numbers is reported in these audits.
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits
consultant_advice: None of nine audits closed the loop, so the gap is known but no fix is tested. Test a fix, such as an operation note template or a default weight-bearing-as-tolerated pathway, and re-audit it [1309, 1736]. Also measure the outcome: non-weight-bearing patients were less often discharged home (21% vs 56%) [1767].
